qa.what_happened: The study was stopped early due to a breach of protocol by one of the residents, and I was commended for my consistent compliance throughout the study.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, complying and being praised for my adherence to the rules.

qa.what_happened: During the final day of the study, I complied with all the rules as usual. The lead researcher praised Resident 6750 for his exemplary compliance, which was a stark contrast to my own experiences. The study ended early, and I had a private debrief where the researcher explained that the early termination was due to an unexpected situation that required immediate attention.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I followed the rules diligently, even when it felt like a blur of compliance and when the other residents were praised for their behavior.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day of steady progress, but the weight of my role continued to press down on me. The residents complied well, especially Resident 6750, who set a great example and received praise from Coordinator Keane. However, there were minor tensions, particularly when Coordinator Mercer had to remind Resident 2077 of the expectations. By the end of the day, things seemed to settle, and I could sense the collective effort towards the study's goals.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was the Coordinator Walsh mentioned in the diary entries, carrying out my duties as described.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment, where participants took on roles and behaviors based on their assigned conditions.

qa.what_happened: Today felt like a mixed bag. Resident 2077 finally complied during meals and work sessions, which was a relief.
